title: The Arctic’s oldest sea ice shrank from a quarter of the pack to 7% in 25 years
body: Sea ice that survives the summer melt keeps thickening year after year: multi-year ice can grow [up to 4 m thick](https://svs.gsfc.nasa.gov/4750/), while ice from a single winter is generally at most 2 m. So as old ice disappears, the pack gets thinner and easier to melt. In 1988, ice at least **4 years old** made up 26% of the Arctic’s sea ice; by 2013 it was only 7%. A 2018 study found the ice had thinned by about 2 metres, or 66%, over six decades.

slides.question: In which year did Arctic sea ice reach its record-low summer minimum, about 3.4 million km²?
slides.explanation: The record lowest minimum, 3,410,000 km², came in September 2012.
